back_translation: The burden-oracle concerning the Wilderness of the Sea: Like whirlwinds sweeping through the Negev, the invader comes from the wilderness, from a terrifying land.
A cruel vision has been declared to me: the traitor still betrays, and the destroyer still destroys. Go up, O Elam! Lay siege, O Media! All the groaning she has caused, I will bring to an end.
Therefore my loins are filled with searing anguish; pangs have seized me, like the pangs of a woman in labor. I am too dazed to hear, too terrified to see.
My heart staggers; horror overwhelms me. The twilight I once longed for has been turned into trembling for me.
They set the table, they spread the rugs, they eat and drink — Rise up, you princes! Oil the shields!
For the Sovereign Master says this to me: "Go, station a watchman; let him report what he sees.
When he sees a column of chariots with pairs of horsemen, a column of donkey-riders, a column of camel-riders, let him listen attentively — most attentively."
Then the watchman cried out: "My lord, I stand on the watchtower all day, every day, and I keep my post throughout every night.
Behold, here comes a column of men on horseback, in pairs!" And one answered and said: "Fallen, fallen is Babylon! And all the carved images of her gods lie shattered on the ground!"
O my people, threshed on the threshing floor! What I have heard from the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, I have declared to you.
The burden-oracle concerning Dumah: Someone calls to me from Seir: "Watchman, how much longer is the night? Watchman, how much longer is the night?"
The watchman replies: "Morning is coming — and the night also. If you would ask, then ask. Turn back, and come again."
The burden-oracle concerning Arabia: You must camp overnight in the thickets of Arabia, O caravans of the Dedanites.
Bring water for the thirsty, O inhabitants of the land of Tema; bring food to welcome the refugees.
For they have fled from the sword — from the sword already drawn, from the bow already bent, and from the crushing weight of war.
For the Sovereign Master says this to me: "Within one year, counted like the years of a hired worker, all the glory of Kedar will come to an end.
And the archers who remain, the warriors of the sons of Kedar, will be very few." For the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken.
